detailed_rationale:
KRBL is the world's largest branded basmati rice exporter, fully integrated from seed development and contract farming through milling, packaging and marketing under the globally-recognized "India Gate" brand, with the largest rice-milling capacity in Punjab. The balance sheet is a clear strength - the company has reduced debt and is now almost debt-free - and profitability has genuinely recovered through FY26: quarterly net profit rose from Rs.87 Cr (Jun-2024) to a run-rate of Rs.151-172 Cr through most of FY26, taking full-year FY26 profit to roughly Rs.648 Cr versus ~Rs.477 Cr in FY25, a ~36% increase. That said, the momentum cooled into year-end - profit peaked at Rs.172 Cr in Q2 FY26 (Sep-2025) and eased to Rs.170 Cr (Dec-2025) and Rs.155 Cr (Mar-2026), essentially flat year-on-year in the final quarter (Rs.154 Cr in Mar-2025) after 30-70% YoY growth earlier in the year - the deceleration is real, though this looks more like normal agri-processing seasonality/base-effect fading than a collapse, since full-year profit still grew handsomely.

Valuation is undemanding: PE of ~13.2x, ROE ~11.7% and ROCE ~15.2% - the screener Cons flag "poor 5-year sales growth (8.84%)" and "low ROE (11.2% 3-yr avg)", which is exactly why the quant quality score sits low (27.6) despite the debt-free balance sheet and category leadership; but a 13x multiple already prices in that modest-growth, modest-ROE reality (our value_score is ~90th percentile - genuinely cheap). Promoter holding is rock-stable at 60.17% since Sep-2023 with no pledge disclosed, FIIs have been adding (3.73% to 7.29%), and recent company activity is routine product-line expansion (India Gate Biryani Kit, India Gate Poha) rather than anything distressed. I found no export-ban, GST, or governance-controversy items in what I could verify - none should be assumed without a source.

Reverse-DCF: at ~13x earnings for a debt-free, branded, cash-generative category leader that just grew profit ~36% for the year (even after a soft Q4), the multiple looks more cheap than fair - the stock is priced closer to a no-growth agri-commodity trader than a branded FMCG exporter with pricing power, which is a mismatch in KRBL's favor.
recommendation_rationale: The quant 1-year score reads Sell (final_score_1y ~36.7), pulled down by a low quality_score (27.6, reflecting sub-15% ROE and modest 5-year sales growth) and a growth_1y_score that captures the second-half deceleration. But the fuller picture argues for a rescue to Hold: full-year FY26 profit still grew ~36%, the balance sheet is debt-free, promoter holding and FII interest are both stable-to-rising, and the stock trades cheaply (~13x PE, ~90th-percentile value score) for a global category leader - the valuation already reflects the modest-ROE reality the quant score is penalizing. This is a genuine rescue case, not a mismatch: I am converting the score-Sell to Hold with this written reason, per the asymmetric-override rule.
summary: KRBL is the world's largest branded basmati rice exporter (India Gate), with a debt-free balance sheet and a full year of strong profit growth (+36%) that cooled somewhat in the most recent quarter. The stock trades cheaply relative to its category leadership and cash generation. On balance we rate it a Hold: the valuation already compensates for the modest returns on equity, and the underlying business remains debt-free and profitable, even as growth momentum has slowed into year-end.
positive_para: KRBL is debt-free, dominates global branded basmati exports through the India Gate franchise, and just delivered ~36% full-year profit growth. The stock is cheap on almost any lens - ~13x earnings, promoter holding stable at over 60% with FIIs adding - and new product launches (biryani kits, poha) show the brand extending into adjacent packaged-food categories rather than standing still. For a debt-free, cash-generative category leader, this valuation leaves real room for a re-rating if growth reaccelerates.
negative_para: The deceleration into Q4 FY26 is the honest concern - profit growth went from +70% YoY in the first quarter of the year to essentially flat by the fourth, and quarter-on-quarter profit has now declined for two consecutive quarters (Rs.172 Cr to Rs.170 Cr to Rs.155 Cr). Five-year sales growth of under 9% and a 3-year ROE averaging just 11.2% are genuinely middling for a scorecard purpose, and basmati rice remains exposed to paddy-price cycles, monsoon variability and export-policy risk that can move faster than quarterly disclosures reveal. The cheap multiple is warranted, not necessarily a bargain, until growth clearly reaccelerates from its current soft patch.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~13x trailing earnings, the market is pricing KRBL closer to a low-growth agri-commodity business than a branded, debt-free global category leader with double-digit full-year profit growth - modestly cheap rather than fair, let alone rich. Growth is well below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
